stories.title: Universities lean on adaptability as AI disrupts career paths
stories.summary: University leaders are shifting focus toward general capabilities as artificial intelligence threatens to upend professional fields. UNSW Sydney deputy vice chancellor Sarah Maddison says the future impact of AI remains unknown, prompting a move away from discipline-specific skills toward broader attributes. Nobody knows what the future holds.

stories.title: Consultants rank community problem-solving as top extracurricular
stories.summary: College applicants are being advised to move beyond common activities to stand out. Educational consultants suggest that activities shared by thousands of students offer diminishing returns. Solving a real-world community problem is currently ranked as the most valuable extracurricular for top-tier university admissions.

stories.title: India looks to 2047 with focus on AI-ready education
stories.summary: India is re-evaluating its education system to prepare students for an economy driven by automation and artificial intelligence. Institutions are aiming to balance technological integration with human development. The country's long-term success is now being tied to its ability to adapt to rapid technological change.

stories.title: Parents cut college savings as AI alters job market outlook
stories.summary: Some parents are reducing contributions to 529 savings plans due to concerns about the future value of a degree. Nataliya Konovalova halved her children's college savings, citing the impact of AI on entry-level hiring. The degree is being weighed against the cost of the tuition.

stories.title: India 2047: Rethinking what students need to learn in an AI-driven world
stories.summary: From developing young minds at Tulas International School to integrating technology into higher education at Tulas University, the vision is to prepare students for a world where the ability to think may matter as much as the ability to know. stories.title: Mental health focus grows as student suicide rates remain high
stories.summary: Children's Day 2026 has brought renewed attention to the academic stress facing students in India. The National Crime Records Bureau reported 14,488 student suicides in 2024. Policymakers are now examining how to create supportive environments that prioritize well-being over traditional marks and rankings.

stories.title: India shifts education policy toward holistic development
stories.summary: India's education sector is moving from a focus on enrollment numbers to foundational learning and student well-being. Policy reforms, including the National Education Policy 2020, are driving the transition. The system is attempting to redefine success for the country's young population through new teaching practices.

stories.title: Professors report gap between exam scores and practical skills
stories.summary: University students are struggling with basic practical tasks despite achieving high marks in secondary school exams. Professors note that subjects like accounting are often taught as theory to be memorized rather than applied. Higher education assumes a level of competence that schools are not currently building.

stories.title: Woman in truck that crashed into soccer field, killing 2, won’t face charges - The Washington Post
Falkner High students examine AI in utility careers
stories.summary: Students at Falkner High School recently reviewed how automation and artificial intelligence are reshaping the utility industry. Representatives from the Central Service Association demonstrated new tools used in electric, water, and gas systems. The utility industry is now being presented as a technology-driven career path.

stories.title: Rhodes scholars named for 2027 include AI and space researchers
stories.summary: Thirty-two Americans have been selected as 2027 Rhodes scholars to study at the University of Oxford. The cohort includes students focused on diverse fields ranging from orbital debris cleanup to AI in healthcare. They were chosen from a pool of over 1,000 candidates.

stories.title: Two Duke students selected for Rhodes Scholarships
stories.summary: Duke University seniors Ari Cook and Lucas Wagner have been named 2026 Rhodes scholars. The scholarship provides two years of graduate study at the University of Oxford. Recipients are selected based on leadership, personal integrity, and a commitment to service.

stories.summary: Seniors Ari Cook and Lucas Wagner were among the 32 recipients selected for the 2026 Rhodes Scholarship Ari Cook will graduate in May 2027 with a degree in Public Policy and a certificate in Child Policy Research. stories.title: Five Burlington students earn $3,000 scholarships for post-secondary studies - BurlingtonToday.com
EIU student receives Lincoln Academy recognition
stories.summary: Eastern Illinois University senior Laney Wright has been named a 2026 Student Laureate by the Lincoln Academy of Illinois. The award recognizes academic achievement and community service. Wright received a medallion, a challenge coin, and a scholarship for her contributions to the campus.

stories.title: Journalist Fida Fatima honored for human solidarity reporting
stories.summary: Journalist Fida Fatima has won the HRRF Journalism Award for her reporting on human solidarity and mob violence. Her work focused on the pursuit of justice for victims of attacks. She was selected from a group of finalists including reporters from BBC News Marathi.

stories.title: Medical student selected for international surgical olympiad
stories.summary: Konstantinos Papadopoulos, a third-year medical student at the University of Crete, has been chosen for the International Surgical Skills Olympiad. He is currently training on surgical models while continuing his studies. The competition requires specialized skills in a field he has pursued through volunteer clinical work.

stories.title: Kim Yu-jae places third in short program at ISU Grand Prix
stories.summary: South Korean skater Kim Yu-jae finished third in the short program at the fourth event of the ISU Grand Prix. She trails the second-place skater by 0.32 points. She is now competing for her first senior medal during the upcoming free skating portion of the event.

stories.title: Celebrating students’ excellence in IGCSE - Borneo Bulletin
Fontana students head to Puerto Rico for robotics competition
stories.summary: Fifteen students from the Fontana Unified School District will compete at the World Robot Olympiad in Puerto Rico this December. Six teams qualified for the international event after designing and programming robots at a national competition in Ontario. The Olympiad challenges students ages 8 to 22.

stories.title: Iranian students secure six golds at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: A six-member Iranian team won six gold medals at the 2026 Open World Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The competition, held in the Sirius Federal Territory, involved theoretical, practical, observational, and test rounds for students aged 14 to 18. All stages were conducted in English.

stories.title: Nepal wins first silver medal at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: Nepali students won four medals at the fifth Open World Astronomy Olympiad in Russia, including the country's first-ever silver medal at an international astronomy competition. Riwash Rai secured the silver and was named Diamond of the Team, while three other students earned bronze medals.

stories.title: Nepal claims historic silver at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: Nepali students secured four medals at the fifth Open World Astronomy Olympiad in Russia, marking the country's first silver medal at an international astronomy event. Riwash Rai took silver and the Diamond of the Team title, while Omraj Puri, Sneha Koirala, and Suyash Koirala won bronze.

stories.summary: All six members of Iran's national B team won gold medals at the fifth Open World Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The competition, held in the Sirius Federal Territory from November 6 to 14, featured students from across the globe competing in various scientific rounds.

stories.title: Biology olympiad medalist returns to teach in Vietnam
stories.summary: Nguyen Dac Hieu, a 2016 International Biology Olympiad bronze medalist, has returned to teach at Lam Son High School for the Gifted in Vietnam. Hieu, 28, was one of over 700 teachers recently appointed by the province to lead specialized biology classes.

stories.title: CBSE releases 2026-27 mathematics sample papers
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has published sample papers for the 2026-27 Class 12 mathematics board examinations. The materials include marking schemes and solutions intended to help students understand the exam pattern, question types, and time management strategies for the upcoming assessment.

stories.title: CBSE makes English core sample paper available for 2027
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the Class 12 English Core sample question paper for the 2026-27 academic session. The document outlines the examination structure, section-wise weightage, and marking scheme for students preparing for the upcoming board examinations.

stories.title: CBSE publishes applied mathematics sample papers for 2027
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released sample question papers and marking schemes for the 2026-27 academic session. Students are advised to distinguish between the separate papers for Mathematics and Applied Mathematics when preparing for the 2027 board examinations.

stories.title: CBSE releases English MCQs for class 10 pre-board exams
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has provided a set of 50 multiple-choice questions for the 2027 Class 10 English pre-board examinations. The material covers reading, grammar, and literature to assist students in their preparation for the secondary school curriculum.

stories.title: CBSE releases physical education sample paper for 2027
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the Class 12 physical education sample question paper for the 2026-27 session. The 70-mark theory exam consists of 37 questions across five sections, including multiple-choice, short-answer, and long-answer formats.

stories.title: CBSE releases computer applications sample paper for 2027
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the Class 10 computer applications sample question paper for the 2026-27 academic session. The document includes the exam pattern, section-wise marks distribution, and sample questions regarding HTML programming.

stories.title: CBSE releases 2026-27 physics sample paper
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has published its Class 12 physics sample paper for the 2026-27 session. The document outlines a 70-mark theory examination spanning three hours and 33 questions. It is designed to help students understand how questions will be asked in the upcoming board examination.

stories.title: CISCE announces 2027 exam schedule
stories.summary: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations has released the 2027 timetable for Class 10 and Class 12. Examinations begin on 15 February and conclude on 31 March. The first paper for Class 10 students is English language paper 1, while the final paper is Group II elective.

stories.title: Prue Leith discusses life after Bake Off
stories.summary: Former Great British Bake Off judge Prue Leith has spoken about her departure from the show after nearly a decade. She cited the filming schedule as a barrier to taking summer holidays. Leith described the experience as leaving her feeling lonely, calling it one of the regrets of her life.

stories.title: Physics Wallah offers discount on math batch
stories.summary: Physics Wallah is offering a 27 percent discount on its Indian Olympiad Qualifier in Mathematics 2027 batch as part of a Children's Day promotion. The price has been reduced from 4,116 to 2,999. The offer is available for a limited period through the official company website.

stories.title: Students compete in writing contest without AI
stories.summary: Science and engineering students are participating in the Joseon Baekil contest alongside humanities peers. The event focuses on evaluating critical thinking and writing skills without the assistance of artificial intelligence. It serves as a test of student capability in a traditional academic format.

stories.title: Abdullah School Organises Science, Mathematics and English Olympiads - India Education Diary
SOF releases 2026-27 general knowledge answer key
stories.summary: The Science Olympiad Foundation has released the answer key for the 2026-27 International General Knowledge Olympiad. Students can download the Set A PDF from the official website to compare against their OMR sheets. Results are expected between December 2026 and January 2027.

stories.title: Kolkata school team wins national chess title
stories.summary: The under-19 boys team from Bhavan's Gangabux Kanoria Vidyamandir in Kolkata won the CBSE National Chess Championship for the second consecutive year. The tournament took place in Jalandhar, Punjab, from 14 to 18 October. Teams from across India and abroad participated in the event.

stories.title: Maharashtra state schools chess winners named
stories.summary: Veer Dhaval Shah and Hriday Maniar won all seven games in their respective categories to emerge as champions at the Maharashtra State Schools Chess Championship. The three-day event, organised by the Indian Chess School, featured 387 players competing across six FIDE-rated categories in Mumbai.

stories.title: Maharashtra chess championship concludes in Mumbai
stories.summary: The Maharashtra State Schools Chess Championship 2026 concluded at Rustomjee Cambridge International School with 387 participants. Veer Dhaval Shah and Hriday Maniar secured titles by winning every game in their categories. The tournament covered age groups from Under-9 to Under-17 across Open and Girls sections.

stories.title: Singapore-India Hackathon begins for students
stories.summary: Education ministers from Singapore and India launched the fourth Singapore-India Hackathon at Singapore Management University. The event brings together 120 tertiary students to address industry and societal challenges. It is co-organised by the university, the All India Council for Technical Education and the Indian Ministry of Education.

stories.title: UT students use AI to develop financial technology in inaugural FinTech at Rocky Top competition - WBIR
Peruvian student wins international astronomy medals
stories.summary: Jordan Juscamaita Altamirano, 16, has won two international astronomy medals in less than two months. He secured a bronze medal in Vietnam and a silver medal at the 5th Open World Astronomy Olympiad held in Russia. The competition included 70 participants from 14 countries.

stories.title: Carleton University opens prestige scholarship applications
stories.summary: Carleton University is accepting applications for its prestige entrance scholarships for the 2027-28 academic year. Awards are available to students entering undergraduate programs with an admission average of 90 percent or higher. Selection is based on grades, leadership, community service and extracurricular involvement.

stories.title: Erasmus University Rotterdam offers international scholarships
stories.summary: Erasmus University Rotterdam is offering the NL Scholarship for international students from outside the European Economic Area. The program is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. Deadlines for the 2027-28 academic year vary by faculty, with some closing in April 2027.

stories.title: University of Padua announces excellence scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Padua is offering excellence scholarships for international students admitted to English-taught degree programs. Applicants are automatically considered for the award upon applying to an eligible bachelor or master program. The next application deadline for the 2027-28 academic year is 1 March 2027.

stories.title: Erasmus Mundus master program details released
stories.summary: The Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Aquaculture, Environment and Society is a two-year program coordinated by the Scottish Association for Marine Science. Students study in Scotland, Greece and France. The program includes EU funding for 81 scholarships over five years, with courses starting in September 2027.

stories.title: ADB offers master’s scholarships for Auckland study
stories.summary: The Asian Development Bank to Japan Scholarship Program provides funding for master’s degrees at the University of Auckland. The program targets citizens from developing member countries, with the expectation that scholars return home to apply their skills. It remains the only partner institution in New Zealand for the program.

stories.title: Pretoria centre offers human rights master’s scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Pretoria’s Centre for Human Rights offers full scholarships for its one-year LLM programme. The course is supported by the European Union and involves study across 12 partner universities in Africa. Applications for the 2027 intake are currently closed following the July deadline.

stories.title: University of the People funds refugee assessment fees
stories.summary: University of the People is a tuition-free online institution that charges application and assessment fees. Its Emergency Refugee Assistance Scholarship Fund, supported by Fondation Hoffmann, covers these costs for refugees and asylum-seekers. The fund was established to address the global refugee crisis.

stories.title: Lancaster University closes doctoral scholarship round
stories.summary: Lancaster University’s Faculty of Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences offers doctoral scholarships covering tuition and maintenance for PhD applicants. The faculty uses a single application process for both its internal awards and AHRC studentships. The competition for the 2027 intake is currently closed.

stories.title: Guggenheim foundation awards PhD candidates studying violence
stories.summary: The Harry Frank Guggenheim Foundation provides awards to PhD candidates in their final year of dissertation writing. The funding is intended to help students finish their work on time rather than support active research. Applicants must have already completed their fieldwork.

stories.title: Erasmus Mundus scholarship round for GLOBED ends
stories.summary: The GLOBED consortium offers Erasmus Mundus scholarships for its two-year master’s programme on international development. Supported by an Erasmus+ grant, the programme is taught across four European universities. The application period for the 2027 intake is currently closed.

stories.title: Science and merit scholarships open for applications
stories.summary: The Focus Area Science Technology Summer Fellowship is open to students across various science and engineering disciplines with a 65 percent minimum average. Separately, the ONGC Foundation is accepting applications for merit scholarships for students from specific categories enrolled in engineering, medicine, or management programmes.

stories.title: HREF announces 300 additional scholarships for Jammu
stories.summary: The Harbans Roshan Bhalla Educational Foundation has announced 300 new scholarships for the 2026-27 academic session. The funding is intended for financially disadvantaged children attending government schools in the Jammu region. The foundation is currently organizing a 12-day selection drive.

stories.title: BSE Odisha sets Class 10 board exam dates
stories.summary: The Board of Secondary Education in Odisha will conduct Class 10 board examinations from March 12 to March 27, 2027. The 16-day schedule includes the State Open School Certificate and Sanskrit Madhyama exams. Mathematics students will receive an additional 15 minutes to complete their papers.

stories.title: Bar Council of India releases AIBE 22 admit cards
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India has released admit cards for the All India Bar Examination 22. Candidates must use their login credentials to download the documents from the official website. The offline examination is scheduled to take place on November 29, 2026.

stories.title: Rajasthan board postpones exams due to Census
stories.summary: The Rajasthan Board of Secondary Education has postponed its Class 10 and 12 examinations originally scheduled for February 2027. The board cited the upcoming Census as the reason for the change. Revised dates for the examinations have not yet been announced.

stories.title: BCI to release AIBE 22 hall tickets today
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India is scheduled to release admit cards for the All India Bar Examination 22 today. Candidates are required to print the hall ticket to gain entry to the examination centre on November 29. The exact time of the release remains unannounced.

stories.title: KEA publishes KCET 2027 syllabus
stories.summary: The Karnataka Examinations Authority has released the syllabus for the 2027 Undergraduate Common Entrance Test. The documents cover physics, chemistry, mathematics, and biology, detailing topics from the first and second PUC classes. The syllabus includes information on practical and theory sections.

stories.title: IIT Delhi sets JEE Advanced 2027 for May
stories.summary: IIT Delhi has scheduled the JEE Advanced 2027 examination for May 23. The institute has launched a website detailing eligibility criteria, which include qualifying among the top 2.5 lakh candidates in the JEE Main BE and BTech paper. Admission remains subject to age and academic requirements.

stories.title: NTA clarifies category selection for JEE Main
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has issued guidance on category selection for JEE Main 2027 applicants. Indian nationals and NRIs with Aadhaar cards must select the Indian Nationals category, while foreign citizens and OCI cardholders are directed to the Foreign Nationals category.

stories.title: Most foreign medical graduates fail October exam
stories.summary: Results from the October 2026 Foreign Medical Graduate Examination show that 77 percent of candidates failed to meet the qualifying marks. Out of the total participants, 9,354 candidates qualified for medical registration in India. The exam is required for those who earned their MBBS degrees abroad.

stories.title: FMGE results show high failure rate for foreign graduates
stories.summary: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences reported that 77.07 percent of candidates failed the October 2026 Foreign Medical Graduate Examination. Students who complete MBBS degrees abroad must pass this eligibility test to practise medicine in India. The results have disappointed many applicants.

stories.title: Germany moves student visa applications online
stories.summary: The German Embassy in Dhaka is launching a digital application system for student visas on January 1. The initiative replaces the existing appointment waiting list with the government's Consular Services Portal. The embassy says the change aims to make the process more transparent, efficient, and predictable for students.

stories.title: US colleges struggle as international students turn away - Politico
US sees uptick in international student interest
stories.summary: International student interest in US universities rose 40 percent in the week following the November 3 midterm elections, according to Studyportals. This follows a two-year decline in demand and a 19 percent drop in master's enrolments during autumn 2025. Students appear to be responding to political developments.

stories.summary: International students’ interest in studying in the US rose 40% in the week after the November 3 midterm elections, according to Studyportals. stories.title: Canada caps international student arrivals until 2029
stories.summary: Canada has set a target of 150,000 new international student arrivals annually through 2029. The cap is part of the 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan, which limits total temporary resident arrivals to 370,000 per year. International students will constitute 40 percent of these arrivals under the new government framework.

stories.title: German embassy to introduce digital student visa process from January
stories.summary: The German Embassy in Dhaka will introduce a digital application system for student visas from January 1 next year, aiming to reduce appointment waiting times and make the process more transparent and efficient. stories.title: UK student visa applications fall 20 percent
stories.summary: UK student visa applications declined 20 percent over the past year, according to Home Office figures. The drop follows tighter immigration rules, increased visa refusals, and uncertainty regarding post-study work opportunities. A total of 349,900 main applicants sought visas during the period, marking a significant shift in demand.

stories.title: Karnataka introduces AI curriculum for government schools
stories.summary: Karnataka has launched an AI curriculum for Class 9 students across 1,800 government high schools for the 2026-27 academic year. The programme covers Python programming, computer vision, and generative AI. The department is currently recruiting guest teachers to deliver the instruction under the National Skills Qualifications Framework.

stories.title: AI can generate answers. Universities must still build knowledge
stories.summary: Pearson’s AI Readiness: Building the Bridge from Higher Education to Work research surveyed 2711 learners, higher-education leaders and employers across six markets. While 67 per cent described AI-driven workplace change as fast, only 24 per cent believed universities were keeping pace. In Australia, the stakes are economic. Pearson’s Lost in

stories.title: Experts rank AI literacy above new classroom tech
stories.summary: Seventy specialists from 18 countries have ranked AI literacy as the most critical trend for education over the next three years. The experts suggest that understanding how tools function is more important than adopting AI tutors or automated grading software. The focus remains on teaching, not hardware.

stories.title: California teachers union seeks AI classroom moratorium
stories.summary: A California teachers' union has requested that Governor Gavin Newsom halt the use of student-facing generative AI in schools for three years. The union argues that children require stronger protections before the technology is further embedded. Los Angeles Unified has already restricted student access on district devices.

stories.title: Professors urge CSU system to use AI for admin work instead of instruction - Sacramento Bee
California teachers urge 3-year pause on AI use in K-8 schools - Sacramento Bee
Google faces backlash over school AI access
stories.summary: Google plans to block its search engine for schools that opt out of its AI tools. The move has drawn criticism from communities amid a broader debate regarding the role of technology in classrooms. The company has not yet detailed how it will manage the transition for schools.

stories.title: Alpha school data shows math targets missed
stories.summary: Alpha School charges parents up to $75,000 annually for an AI-driven curriculum. Internal data shows only 42% of students met the goal of learning twice as fast in math and reading. The network is now pushing its software into public school districts.

stories.title: AI skills demand grows across Indian sectors
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence is becoming an integral part of India's business, education, and healthcare ecosystems. Organisations are increasingly seeking professionals capable of developing predictive models and automating business processes. The trend has led to a rise in demand for specialized AI training and courses across the country.

stories.title: Expert calls for teacher development in Africa
stories.summary: Dr. Onyekachi Onwudike-Jumbo has advocated for a shift toward sustainable professional development for educators. She maintains that Africa's long-term socioeconomic growth depends on the quality of its teachers. The approach aims to better equip staff to respond to the realities of modern classrooms.

stories.title: Teachers use AI to encourage student confidence
stories.summary: Teachers at Tran Can High School are using AI to help students access knowledge proactively. The tools are designed to provide hints for incorrect answers rather than stopping the learning process. The educators aim to spark interest while ensuring students feel cared for during their growth.

stories.title: South African teachers report development fatigue
stories.summary: Teachers in South Africa are required to complete regular professional development to maintain their credentials. Many educators view these programmes as an unnecessary burden, citing existing challenges like overcrowded classrooms and heavy administrative workloads. The system relies on points endorsed by the national council for educators.

stories.title: Imo State governor promotes AI in education
stories.summary: Governor Hope Uzodimma has identified artificial intelligence as a key tool for 21st-century educational development. Speaking at a conference in Imo State, he emphasized that teachers remain the foundation of the sector. The governor highlighted the need for integrating new technology to support professional growth.

stories.title: Teacher reports high failure rate linked to AI
stories.summary: A secondary school teacher says he must fail 90% of his students after discovering they used AI to complete coursework. The teacher expressed concern over how much knowledge his pupils have actually retained this year. He believes the issue extends beyond the classroom environment.

stories.title: Kenyan teachers await career guideline implementation
stories.summary: Teachers in Kenya have expressed optimism following the approval of new Career Progression Guidelines. President William Ruto announced the move after the Salaries and Remuneration Commission cleared the plan. Educators are now calling for the Teachers Service Commission to implement the changes without further delay.

stories.title: Headteachers urged to focus on foundational skills
stories.summary: Schools are being advised to prioritize early literacy and numeracy over examination results or infrastructure. Experts argue that foundational skills are the building blocks of any successful education system. The focus is intended to ensure children can read and communicate effectively before moving to higher grades.

stories.title: Teachers adapt AI for mountainous regions
stories.summary: Teachers in Thanh Hoa province are exploring how AI can innovate learning in mountainous areas. Educators are testing methods to ensure technology remains suitable for local conditions. During a literature class, students debated the merits of AI-generated essays to better understand the role of the tool.

stories.title: University don warns against replacing teachers
stories.summary: Professor Serifat Labo-Popoola has warned against using technology to displace teachers in English language instruction. She argued that digital tools and AI should only complement the role of educators. The professor called for increased investment in teacher quality to meet emerging demands in the sector.

stories.title: Panchkula school investigates missing student
stories.summary: A six-year-old student went missing from a school in Haryana after being dropped off by an auto-rickshaw. Her family discovered her absence when the driver arrived for pickup and found her bag at the reception. The father has since questioned school staff regarding her whereabouts.

stories.title: Arunachal governor emphasizes teacher training
stories.summary: Governor K.T. Parnaik has highlighted the National Education Policy 2020, which focuses on continuous professional development for teachers. During the inauguration of a new training institute, he stated that competency-based learning objectives can only be realized when educators are adequately trained, motivated, and supported by institutional frameworks.

stories.title: Seminar addresses NEP 2020 implementation in Nagaland
stories.summary: Experts at Patkai Christian College discussed the challenges of implementing the National Education Policy 2020 in Nagaland. The seminar emphasized the need for stronger industry-academia linkages and skill-based learning. Participants examined how to better align institutional support with the policy's requirements for the state's education system.

stories.title: Nepal moves to include climate education
stories.summary: Minister for Education and Sports Sasmit Pokharel announced that a process is underway to integrate climate education into the school curriculum. The initiative is part of a long-term foundation for climate adaptation. The minister shared the update during a high-level session at COP-31 in Turkiye.

stories.title: Somalia integrates climate education into adaptation plan
stories.summary: The Minister of Environment and Climate Change has opened a panel at COP31 to discuss the role of education in Somalia's National Adaptation Plan. The session focused on equipping young people with climate-related knowledge and strengthening institutional cooperation. The initiative aims to build resilience through the national education system.

stories.title: Fiji education sector faces staffing hurdles
stories.summary: Fiji's Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro says the country faces critical shortages in specialised subject areas and a reluctance among teachers to serve in remote communities. These challenges remain a primary focus for the ministry as it works to strengthen the quality and delivery of national education.

stories.title: FCT and EIDU expand digital learning programme
stories.summary: The FCT Education Secretariat and EIDU are expanding their digital learning reform programme to more public primary schools. The initiative integrates artificial intelligence tools and structured pedagogy to improve foundational literacy. The partners have also begun distributing textbooks to 35 schools across the six Area Councils.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning partners with Meru International School
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning has announced a strategic partnership with Meru International School in Hyderabad. The deal combines Meru's inquiry-led philosophy with the academic infrastructure and national network of Lighthouse Learning. The partnership aims to strengthen educational opportunities across the school's existing campuses in Miyapur and Tellapur.

stories.title: Lighthouse Learning acquires stake in Meru International School
stories.summary: Lighthouse Learning, controlled by private equity firm KKR, has acquired a stake in Hyderabad-based Meru International School. The school offers CBSE and Cambridge curricula from early years through grade 12. This marks the third deal this year for the education company, formerly known as EuroKids International.

stories.title: Trump administration ends Head Start pay mandate
stories.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services has issued a final rule rolling back a Biden-era effort to mandate competitive salaries for Head Start staff. The previous policy was designed to reduce high turnover rates within the early education program.

stories.title: Nellore international school set for 2027 opening
stories.summary: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam International School in Nellore is scheduled to open in June 2027. The project is built on a 5-acre plot of Waqf Board land using 20 crore rupees in CSR funds. It aims to provide free corporate education to over 1,000 underprivileged students.

stories.title: Uttarakhand expands state medical and nursing colleges
stories.summary: Uttarakhand has established three new government medical colleges and three government nursing colleges over the past five years. The state now operates six government medical colleges across various districts. The expansion is intended to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and provide more career opportunities for local students.

stories.title: ICSI announces October 2026 entrance test results
stories.summary: The Institute of Company Secretaries of India has released the results for the October 2026 Company Secretary Executive Entrance Test. Bhakti Sanjay Shah secured the first rank, followed by Abhimanyu Singh Rajput and Manjiree Joshi. Candidates can now access their subject-wise marks on the official website.

stories.title: NIFTEE 2027 registration deadline extended
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has extended the registration deadline for the National Institute of Fashion Technology Entrance Examination to November 24, 2026. The extension applies to undergraduate, postgraduate, lateral entry, artisan, and PhD programmes. Late applications will be accepted for an additional fee.

stories.title: Last date for submission of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme for academic year 2026-27
Karimnagar schools host Children's Day events
stories.summary: Paradise and St. George International School in Karimnagar celebrated Children's Day with cultural programmes and skits. Students participated in a morning assembly and dance performances. The event was formally inaugurated by school chairman P. Fathima Reddy, who paid tribute to Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

stories.title: Vignan’s University opens 2027 to 28 admissions
stories.summary: Vignan’s University has announced admissions for its Guntur and Hyderabad campuses. The institution is accepting applications for various undergraduate and postgraduate degrees. The university has integrated artificial intelligence into its curriculum and established a Google AI Lab to support technology-driven learning for its students.

stories.title: St Theresa’s ICSE marks Children’s Day
stories.summary: The high school section of St Theresa’s ICSE School in Mangaluru celebrated Children’s Day with a programme organised by faculty members. The principal encouraged students to cherish their childhood and discover their unique talents. The event included music and festive activities for the students.

stories.title: St Cecily’s CBSE hosts Children’s Day programme
stories.summary: Faculty members at St Cecily’s English Medium Higher Primary School hosted a Children’s Day programme for students. The event featured a decorated stage and a series of entertaining activities performed by the teachers. The day began with an invocatory prayer for children across the world.

stories.title: St Theresa’s ICSE primary section celebrates Children’s Day
stories.summary: The primary section of St Theresa’s ICSE School in Mangaluru celebrated Children’s Day with games, interactive activities, and a dance session for grades 1 to 5. The event was organised to create lasting memories for the students, who were also treated to refreshments.

stories.title: ProTeen launches scholarship for 40 students
stories.summary: ProTeen has opened applications for its Young Achievers Scholarship 2026, offering a cumulative 10 lakh rupees to 40 students. The programme is open to students in classes 10 and 12. Selection is based on interest assessments and essays rather than academic marks alone.

stories.title: Uttarakhand to reopen 12 vocational institutes
stories.summary: Uttarakhand will reopen 12 non-operational Government Industrial Training Institutes in the next academic session. The state aims to provide vocational and technical training closer to home for local youth. Officials have been directed to complete the necessary formalities to boost skill development and employment prospects.
